turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure. I'll solve one example and say what I'm thinking.
I work in a hotel. She works in a hotel.
Step 1: Who is the subject? "She" - one person, not me or you.
Step 2: So I add -s to the verb: works.
The rule in one line: after he, she or it, add -s to the verb.
Right: My brother works there. Wrong: My brother work there.

Now try this one. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
